title: Complete flag bundle by tautological kernels
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $r\in\mathbf N$, and $F$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_T$-module of constant rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Pullback of modules is [def-pc-module-pullback], and an invertible module means [def-sc-invertible-module]. Define the complete flag bundle $p:\operatorname{Fl}_T(F)\to T$, together with its filtration, by recursion on $r$. For $r=0$ take $p=\operatorname{id}_T$ and $F_0=0=F$; for $r=1$ take $p=\operatorname{id}_T$ and $0=F_0\subset F_1=F$. For $r>1$, form $q:P=\mathbf P_T(F)=\operatorname{Proj}_T\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}F\to T$ and $L=\mathcal O_P(1)$ as in [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry]. Use the quotient-line convention: the degree-one generators give the map $\epsilon:q^*F\to L$. In a frame $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ of $F$, on $D_+(X_j)$ with twist generator $\tau_j$ its formula is $\epsilon(v_i)=(X_i/X_j)\tau_j$. These formulas define the same map on overlaps: $\tau_j=(X_j/X_k)\tau_k$, and a change of frame acts on degree-one generators of $\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}F$ by that same change of basis. Define $K=\ker\epsilon$, the subsheaf of sections sent to zero. On this chart $\epsilon$ has section $\tau_j\mapsto v_j$, and $K$ has basis $v_i-(X_i/X_j)v_j$ for $i\ne j$; thus $K$ has rank $r-1$ and this recursive call is defined. Put $T'=\operatorname{Fl}_P(K)$, write $h:T'\to P$ for its recursively defined projection, and set $p=q\circ h$. If $0=G_0\subset\cdots\subset G_{r-1}=h^*K$ is the recursive filtration, set $F_i=G_i\subset h^*q^*F=p^*F$ for $0\le i\le r-1$, using the pullback of the inclusion $K\subset q^*F$, and set $F_r=p^*F$. Its last quotient is $Q_r=h^*L$; the earlier quotients are $Q_i=G_i/G_{i-1}$. Quotients here are sheaf quotients. This recursively specified filtration is called the universal filtration. Each $Q_i$ is invertible, and each $F_i$ is a vector subbundle, meaning that $p^*F/F_i$ is locally free. Indeed the displayed chart splitting remains a splitting after pullback; combining it with an adapted frame for the recursive filtration gives an adapted local frame for the new filtration. No splitting on all of $T'$ is part of the data.
